Tulsi.description: An aromatic shrub native to the Indian subcontinent, widely grown in households and considered sacred in Indian tradition. Recognized by its fragrant green or purple leaves.
traditional_uses: Commonly used in Indian traditional medicine
Respiratory comfort (traditionally used in herbal teas)
Digestive support
General wellness and immunity support
precautions: May interact with blood-thinning or diabetes medication
Not confirmed safe in medicinal doses during pregnancy
Consult a qualified practitioner before regular consumption

Neem.description: A fast-growing tree with bitter-tasting compound leaves, widely used in traditional skincare and pest-control practices across South Asia.
traditional_uses: Traditionally applied for skin comfort
Used in oral care preparations (neem twigs)
Reported use as a natural pest deterrent
precautions: Neem oil/seed extracts are toxic if ingested, especially by children
Not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding
Avoid prolonged undiluted skin contact

Aloe Vera.description: A succulent plant with thick, fleshy, serrated leaves containing a clear gel, popular in skincare and traditional remedies.
traditional_uses: Traditionally applied on skin for soothing comfort
Used in traditional preparations for minor burns
Reported use in hair-care formulations
precautions: Oral consumption of aloe latex may cause digestive upset
Perform a patch test before topical use
Avoid ingestion without professional guidance

Ashwagandha.description: A small shrub with oval leaves and yellow flowers; its root is a well-known ingredient in traditional Ayurvedic formulations.
traditional_uses: Traditionally used to support stress resilience
Reported use for general vitality and energy
Used in traditional sleep-support formulations
precautions: May affect thyroid hormone levels
Not recommended during pregnancy
May interact with sedatives and immunosuppressants

Turmeric.description: A rhizomatous herbaceous plant whose bright yellow-orange root is a staple in South Asian cooking and traditional medicine.
traditional_uses: Widely used as a culinary spice
Traditionally applied for skin comfort
Reported use for general wellness and digestive support
precautions: High doses may cause digestive discomfort
May increase bleeding risk with anticoagulants
Use caution if prone to kidney stones

Ginger.description: A flowering plant whose aromatic rhizome is used extensively as a spice and in traditional remedies for digestive comfort.
traditional_uses: Traditionally used for digestive and nausea comfort
Common ingredient in herbal teas
Reported use for general warmth/circulation support
precautions: May interact with blood-thinning medication
High doses may cause heartburn
Consult a doctor before use in gallstone conditions

Amla.description: Also known as Indian gooseberry, a small to medium tree bearing round, green, sour fruit rich in traditional nutritional reputation.
traditional_uses: Traditionally valued as a source of Vitamin C
Reported use in hair-care formulations
Used in traditional digestive tonics
precautions: May lower blood sugar levels
Use caution alongside diabetes medication
Excess consumption may cause acidity in sensitive individuals

Giloy.description: A climbing shrub with heart-shaped leaves, commonly used in traditional Indian medicine and known for its bitter stem.
traditional_uses: Traditionally used for general immunity support
Reported use during recovery from common ailments
Used in traditional fever-management formulations
precautions: May lower blood sugar - caution with diabetes medication
Not well-studied for long-term/high-dose safety
Avoid self-medicating for serious illness

Mint.description: A fast-spreading aromatic herb with serrated leaves and a cooling flavor, commonly used in food and traditional remedies.
traditional_uses: Traditionally used for digestive comfort
Common flavoring in herbal teas and food
Reported use for freshening breath
precautions: Undiluted mint oil can irritate skin and mucous membranes
May worsen acid reflux in some individuals
Use caution giving mint oil to infants

Lemongrass.description: A tall, tufted tropical grass with a citrus aroma, widely used in cooking, teas, and traditional remedies.
traditional_uses: Commonly brewed as an herbal tea
Traditionally reported for digestive comfort
Used in traditional aromatic preparations
precautions: Essential oil should not be taken undiluted
May cause skin irritation in concentrated form
Limited safety data for pregnancy - use caution

Moringa.description: Known as the 'drumstick tree', a fast-growing tree with small round leaves valued for its nutrient-dense leaves and pods.
traditional_uses: Traditionally valued as a nutrient-rich food source
Reported use for general wellness support
Used in traditional formulations for energy
precautions: Root and bark extracts may be unsafe - avoid without guidance
May lower blood sugar and blood pressure
Use caution during pregnancy

Brahmi.description: A small creeping herb that thrives in wet, marshy areas, with succulent oblong leaves used in traditional cognitive-support formulations.
traditional_uses: Traditionally used to support memory and focus
Reported use in traditional relaxation formulations
Used in traditional hair-care oils
precautions: May cause digestive upset in some individuals
May interact with thyroid or sedative medication
Effects may take weeks of consistent traditional use to notice

Arjuna.description: A large evergreen tree with a distinctive smooth, grey bark that peels in flakes; the bark is prominent in traditional heart-health formulations.
traditional_uses: Traditionally used in heart-health-related formulations
Reported use for general cardiovascular wellness support
Used in traditional preparations for stamina
precautions: Not a substitute for prescribed heart medication
May interact with blood pressure or heart medications
Consult a cardiologist before use if you have a heart condition

Curry Leaf.description: A small tree/shrub with aromatic compound leaves widely used as a flavoring agent in South Asian cuisine.
traditional_uses: Widely used as a culinary flavoring herb
Traditionally reported use for digestive support
Used in traditional hair-care preparations
precautions: Generally regarded as safe in culinary amounts
High medicinal doses not well studied
Consult a practitioner before therapeutic use

Shatavari.description: A climbing, thorny plant with needle-like leaves and tuberous roots, traditionally significant in women's wellness formulations.
traditional_uses: Traditionally used in women's wellness formulations
Reported use for general vitality support
Used in traditional digestive tonics
precautions: May interact with hormone-related medication
Avoid in individuals allergic to asparagus
Consult a practitioner before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding
